Everyone wants good friends.
How can you be a good friend? Here are four {{v:tips}}.
First, {{g:listen well|명령문: 동사원형으로 시작해서 '~해라'}}.
Look at your friend. {{g:Don't stop your friend in the middle|부정 명령문: Don't + 동사원형 = ~하지 마라}}.
Second, {{v:share}} with your friends.
You can share your {{v:snacks}}, books, or your time.
Then your friends will be happy.
Third, keep {{v:secrets}}.
Your friend tells you a secret. Don't tell other people.
Then your friend {{g:will trust you|will + 동사원형: ~할 것이다 (미래)}}.
Last, say sorry for your {{v:mistakes}}.
Everyone makes mistakes.
You may not want to say sorry. But it is very important.
Also, {{v:forgive}} your friend.
A good friend is like a special gift.
{{t:Be a good friend. Then you will have good friends, too!}}

Everyone wants good friends. But how can you be a good friend? Here are four {{v:tips}}.
First, listen {{v:carefully}}. {{g:When your friend talks|접속사 when: ~할 때}}, look at your friend and don't {{v:interrupt}}.
Second, share with your friends. You can share your snacks, books, or even your time. {{g:Sharing makes friends happy|동명사 주어(Sharing) + make + 목적어 + 형용사: ~을 …하게 만들다}}.

A good friend is like a special {{v:present}}. {{t:If you are a good friend, you will have good friends, too!}}

Everyone wants good friends. But how can you become a good friend yourself? Here are four {{v:helpful}} tips.
First, listen carefully. When your friend is talking, look at your friend's face and {{g:try not to interrupt|try not to + 동사원형: ~하지 않으려고 노력하다 (to부정사의 부정)}}. {{g:This shows that you truly care about your friend's feelings|접속사 that: ~라는 것 (명사절)}}.
Second, share with your friends. You can share your snacks, your books, or even your free time. {{g:Sharing makes your friends feel happy and special|사역동사 make + 목적어 + 동사원형: ~가 …하게 하다}}.
Third, keep secrets. If your friend tells you a secret, don't tell it to anyone else. Then your friend will know that you are {{v:trustworthy}}.
Finally, {{v:apologize}} when you make a mistake. Everyone makes mistakes sometimes. Saying sorry is not easy, but it is {{g:one of the most important things|one of the + 최상급 + 복수명사: 가장 ~한 것들 중 하나}} in a {{v:friendship}}. Also, be {{v:ready}} to forgive your friend when they say sorry to you.
A good friend is like a special present {{g:that you can keep forever|관계대명사 that: 앞의 명사(present)를 꾸밈}}. {{t:If you try to be a good friend, you will have good friends, too!}}

prestudy.tagged_body:
Almost everyone hopes to have good friends, but not many people stop to think about {{g:what being a good friend actually requires|의문사 what이 이끄는 명사절 (간접의문문) + 동명사 주어 being}}. Here are four {{v:practical}} tips that anyone can follow.
First, be a careful listener. Whenever your friend is speaking, make eye contact and {{g:avoid interrupting|avoid + 동명사: ~하는 것을 피하다}}, even if you are {{v:eager}} to share your own thoughts. Listening {{v:patiently}} shows your friend that their words truly matter to you.
Second, be {{v:generous}} with your friends. You might share your snacks or your favorite books, but {{g:the most valuable thing you can offer|최상급 + 목적격 관계대명사 생략 (thing (that) you can offer)}} is your time. Sharing what you have makes your friends feel {{v:appreciated}}.
Third, keep the secrets that your friends trust you with. If a friend tells you something {{v:private}}, never pass it on to anyone else. {{g:Only a person who can keep a secret will be trusted completely|주격 관계대명사 who + 조동사 수동태 will be + 과거분사}}.
Finally, apologize {{v:sincerely}} whenever you make a mistake. Nobody is perfect, and everyone makes mistakes from time to time. {{g:Although saying sorry is never easy|although: 비록 ~이지만 (양보의 접속사)}}, it is one of the most {{v:essential}} parts of any friendship. Likewise, be willing to forgive your friend when they apologize to you.
A true friend is like a precious gift that lasts a lifetime. {{t:If you make the effort to be a good friend, you will surely find good friends in return!}}

questions.explanation: 'not many people stop to think about what being a good friend actually requires'는 좋은 친구가 되려면 무엇이 필요한지 생각해 보는 사람이 많지 않다는 뜻이다.

questions.answer: Look at the other person's eyes
questions.explanation: make eye contact는 '눈을 맞추다', 즉 상대방의 눈을 바라본다는 뜻이다.

questions.q: Which is closest in meaning to 'eager' in the passage?
questions.explanation: be eager to는 '몹시 ~하고 싶어 하다'라는 뜻이다. 자기 생각을 말하고 싶더라도 말을 끊지 말라는 내용이다.

questions.q: According to the writer, what is the most valuable thing you can share?
questions.explanation: 'the most valuable thing you can offer is your time'과 일치한다.

questions.q: Which is closest in meaning to 'generous'?
questions.explanation: generous는 '너그러운, 아낌없이 주는'이라는 뜻이다. 뒤에 나누는 내용이 이어진다.

questions.q: Choose the word that best fits the blank: Only a person who can keep a secret will ____ trusted completely.
questions.explanation: 조동사 will 뒤에는 동사원형이 오므로, 수동태는 'will be + 과거분사(trusted)'가 된다.

questions.q: What does 'never pass it on to anyone else' mean?
choices: Never tell the secret to other people.
questions.answer: Never tell the secret to other people.
questions.explanation: pass on은 '(다른 사람에게) 전하다'라는 뜻이다. 친구의 비밀을 다른 누구에게도 전하지 말라는 뜻이다.

questions.q: Choose the word that best fits the blank: ____ saying sorry is never easy, it is one of the most essential parts of any friendship.
questions.explanation: '사과하는 것은 쉽지 않지만, 우정에서 가장 중요한 부분 중 하나이다'라는 반대 내용이 이어지므로 양보의 접속사 Although가 알맞다.

questions.q: Which sentence supports the idea that everyone makes mistakes?
questions.explanation: 'Nobody is perfect, and everyone makes mistakes from time to time.'에서 '완벽한 사람은 없다'가 누구나 실수한다는 생각을 뒷받침한다.

questions.q: Which is NOT true according to the passage?
choices: You should avoid interrupting your friend.
Sharing makes your friends feel appreciated.
You should share only things, not your time.
Everyone makes mistakes from time to time.
You should be willing to forgive your friend.
questions.answer: You should share only things, not your time.
questions.explanation: 글쓴이는 나눌 수 있는 가장 소중한 것이 시간이라고 했으므로 사실이 아니다.

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Good friends never argue with each other.
It is better to have many friends than a few.
Being a good friend takes effort, and it brings good friends in return.
Presents are the best way to make friends.
You should keep your own thoughts secret.
questions.answer: Being a good friend takes effort, and it brings good friends in return.
questions.explanation: 마지막 문장 'If you make the effort to be a good friend, you will surely find good friends in return!'이 글의 요지이다.

questions.q: Whenever your friend is speaking, make eye contact and avoid ____.
questions.explanation: 'make eye contact and avoid interrupting'에서 확인할 수 있다. avoid 뒤에는 동명사가 온다.

questions.q: The most ____ thing you can offer is your time.
questions.explanation: 'the most valuable thing you can offer is your time'에서 확인할 수 있다.

questions.q: If a friend tells you something ____, never pass it on to anyone else.
questions.explanation: 'If a friend tells you something private'에서 확인할 수 있다. private은 '사적인, 비밀의'라는 뜻이다.

questions.q: Finally, apologize ____ whenever you make a mistake.
questions.explanation: 'apologize sincerely whenever you make a mistake'에서 확인할 수 있다. sincerely는 '진심으로'라는 뜻이다.

questions.q: A true friend is like a precious gift that lasts a ____.
questions.explanation: 'a precious gift that lasts a lifetime'에서 확인할 수 있다.

questions.q: The writer says you may interrupt your friend if you are eager to share your thoughts.
questions.explanation: 'avoid interrupting, even if you are eager to share your own thoughts'라고 했으므로 말하고 싶어도 끊으면 안 된다.

questions.q: The writer believes everyone makes mistakes from time to time.
questions.explanation: 'everyone makes mistakes from time to time'과 일치한다.

questions.q: You should be willing to forgive a friend who apologizes to you.
questions.explanation: 'be willing to forgive your friend when they apologize to you'와 일치한다.

items: Only a person who can keep a secret will be trusted completely.
Listening patiently shows your friend that their words truly matter to you.
Likewise, be willing to forgive your friend when they apologize to you.
Sharing what you have makes your friends feel appreciated.
answer: Listening patiently shows your friend that their words truly matter to you.
Sharing what you have makes your friends feel appreciated.
Only a person who can keep a secret will be trusted completely.
Likewise, be willing to forgive your friend when they apologize to you.

essays.q: Explain in English why listening patiently is important in a friendship.
essays.sampleAnswer: It is important because it shows your friend that their words truly matter to you.
essays.rubric: 친구의 말이 나에게 정말 중요하다는 것을 보여 준다는 내용이 들어가면 만점

essays.q: Rewrite the sentence in the passive voice: People will trust only a person who can keep a secret.
essays.sampleAnswer: Only a person who can keep a secret will be trusted.
essays.rubric: will be trusted (조동사 수동태) 구조를 바르게 쓰면 만점

essays.q: 우리말로 쓰시오: 글쓴이는 친구와 나눌 수 있는 가장 소중한 것이 무엇이라고 했나요? 그것이 왜 소중한지 자신의 생각을 덧붙여 쓰시오.
essays.sampleAnswer: 시간이다. 시간은 한 번 쓰면 돌아오지 않기 때문에, 친구와 함께 시간을 보내는 것은 그 친구를 아낀다는 뜻이 되기 때문이다.
essays.rubric: '시간'을 정확히 쓰고 알맞은 이유를 덧붙이면 만점, '시간'만 쓰면 부분 점수

essays.q: What does the writer mean by 'you will surely find good friends in return'? Write in English.
essays.sampleAnswer: If you are a good friend to others, they will be good friends to you, too.
essays.rubric: 내가 좋은 친구가 되면 그 보답으로 좋은 친구가 생긴다는 의미를 영어로 쓰면 만점

essays.q: 우리말로 쓰시오: 이 글의 네 가지 조언을 각각 한 가지 구체적인 행동과 함께 쓰시오.
essays.sampleAnswer: ① 잘 듣기 – 눈을 맞추고 말을 끊지 않는다. ② 나누기 – 간식, 책, 시간을 나눈다. ③ 비밀 지키기 – 친구의 비밀을 다른 사람에게 전하지 않는다. ④ 사과하기 – 실수하면 진심으로 사과하고, 친구가 사과하면 용서한다.
essays.rubric: 네 가지 조언과 각각의 구체적 행동을 모두 쓰면 만점, 조언만 쓰거나 일부만 쓰면 부분 점수
